newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish external reserves up 40 mln punts in February.
newsitem.headline: Irish external reserves up 40 mln punts in February.

text.p: Ireland's official external reserves rose by 40 million Irish pounds to 5.81 billion at the end of February, central bank monthly statistics showed on Thursday.
The main item adding to the reserves was EU receipts and there were also modest net positive foreign exchange market interventions, the central bank said in a statement.

But the bank said the extent of the increase in the reserves was reduced by interest and principal payments on the Exchequer foreign debt and there was also a valuation adjustment which reduced the Irish-pound value of the reserves.
The central bank said credit to the government increased by 189 million Irish pounds due to an increase in banks' holding of government bonds.
Non-resident holdings of Irish government securities fell by 131 million.
With Irish-pound funding and EU receipts exceeding net government expenditure and foreign currency debt repayments, government balances at the central bank increased by 47 million, the bank said.
